title: Longmen Grottoes
summary: The Longmen Grottoes are a Buddhist cave complex on both banks of the Yi River south of Luoyang, Henan. Carving began in 493 after the Northern Wei capital moved to Luoyang and was most intense until the mid-8th century. More than 2,300 caves and niches hold almost 110,000 statues; the Tang-era Fengxian Cave was completed in 675.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia says carving ran about five centuries from 493; UNESCO says the most intensive period ran from the end of the 5th century to the mid-8th century, taken here as 750.

importance.justification: UNESCO calls its carvings the high point of Chinese stone sculpture, spanning the late Northern Wei and Tang dynasties.
